source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #349 (branch fix/335-handle-validation at head d8e85b95f4a61642e1f22a90b2f0f184ca03b72b — the #335 change (canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table) with the Codex-review follow-up (host-provided handles pass through on a local-index collision, and two synthetic import-path identities of one provider resource are not distinguished at the boundary), merged with current main d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3 (PR #350); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45592728395 and 45592737968 against the branch and pull-request run 45592732867, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #349 (#335, canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table; second re-baseline for this PR, after the Codex-review follow-up commit and the merge of PR #350 (#330) into the branch — merge commit d8e85b9, main at d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3 on top of the 21edef0f0b147af7a43dcbec002673227ff8516d main the first re-baseline (commit 95bea7f) was measured against; the merge conflicted only in the baseline files, resolved by taking main's baseline as the base for this campaign). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45591376361, 45591385117 and 45591392298 on main at d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline). Against the checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on 29 of the 32 gated series; on the three release stripped file series of component, wasi and wasi-threads it measures −32 B, the residual staleness of the PR #350 snapshot (the gate passes shrinkage, so the staleness was inert). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +4,528 B / +4,528 B / +4,512 B and stripped .text +3,456 B in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads; in release-size, stripped file +3,352 B / +3,368 B / +3,336 B and stripped .text +2,272 B / +2,288 B / +2,272 B. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline and are re-baselined to the branch measurements; every other baseline is unchanged. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +10.47% (2,433,656 B to 2,688,424 B); the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
